column4: 杯子 is the generic word for a drinking cup/glass; "taza" alone narrows it to a handled cup only
platillo is a Mexican-regionalism diminutive; "plato" is the neutral term for a dish/course
会 is the learned-skill "know how to"; keeping "poder" here collides with 能 (w072), which already owns "poder"
看 is the plain act of looking/watching; "ver" belongs to 看见 (w051, "to see/perceive"), so listing it here blurs that distinction
米饭 is just cooked/steamed rice as food; "arroz cocido" is redundant and unnatural — a Spanish speaker just says "arroz"
呢 and 吗 (w060) are both glossed identically as "(partícula interrogativa)"; 呢 is specifically the follow-up/confirmation particle (你呢? = ¿y tú?), so it needs its own tag
